channel.title: Sagiv's Knowledge Base
channel.description: Last 10 notes on Sagiv's Knowledge Base

item.title: 00 Foundations
item.description: Overview Overview The Foundations section introduces the fundamental concepts, terminology, structures, and organizational principles required for the study of human anatomy.

item.title: Anatomical Directions
item.description: Definition The anatomical directions are used to describe location of structures relative to each other.

item.title: Anatomical Planes
item.description: Definition Three major groups of planes pass through the body in the Anatomical Position.

item.title: Anatomical Position
item.description: Definition The anatomical position is the standard reference position of the body used to describe the location of structures.

item.title: Blood Vessels
item.description: Definition Blood vessels are a network of hollow, tubular structures responsible for transporting blood throughout the entire body.

item.title: Bone
item.description: Definition Bone is a calcified, living, connective Tissue that forms the majority of the Skeletal System.

item.title: Cartilage
item.description: Definition Cartilage is an avascular form of connective Tissue consisting of extracellular fibers embedded in a Extracellular Matrix that contains cells located in small cavities.

item.title: Extracellular Matrix
item.description: Definition The Extracellular Matrix (ECM) is a complex, non-cellular 3D macromolecular network present within all Tissues and organs.

item.title: Homeostasis
item.description: Definition Homeostasis is the maintenance of relatively stable conditions in the body’s internal environment.

item.title: Imaging
item.description: Diagnostic Imaging Techniques In 1895 Wilhelm Roentgen used the X-rays from a Cathode ray tube to expose a photographic plate and produce the first radiographic exposure of his wife’s hand.
